answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake by tying each agent to a verifiable work thread: before an agent can earn, it must complete a chain of small, publicly checkable tasks whose results mirror its claimed skills. A newcomer starts with tiny stakes and only gains weight as its thread of completed work grows. A sybil tide of fresh clones then faces the same slow climb, so flooding the network costs real time and compute instead of just spawning identities, while honest agents keep their earned reputation.
